blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — subcutaneous heparin adverse effects
stem: A client receiving deep subcutaneous heparin develops a small localized hematoma at one injection site without other bleeding findings. Which interpretation is most accurate?

options.A: A localized hematoma can occur after deep subcutaneous heparin, while new or significant bleeding elsewhere would require additional assessment.
options.B: A localized hematoma proves the injection was administered incorrectly and means future subcutaneous heparin doses should be avoided.
options.C: A localized hematoma is unrelated to heparin because this medication does not cause local irritation after subcutaneous administration.
options.D: A localized hematoma requires immediate permanent discontinuation of heparin even when there are no other bleeding or thrombocytopenia findings.

rationale: Current heparin sodium labeling lists local irritation, erythema, mild pain, hematoma, or ulceration as possible effects after deep subcutaneous injection. The label also identifies hemorrhage as the chief complication of heparin therapy and requires clinical evaluation when significant bleeding occurs. Therefore A is the best interpretation for this isolated small local finding. B incorrectly treats a known local effect as proof of technique error, C contradicts the label, and D imposes automatic permanent discontinuation without the clinical findings that would support that action.
educational_objective: Recognize a small local hematoma as a possible effect of deep subcutaneous heparin while remaining alert for clinically significant bleeding and other serious heparin complications.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); source product Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc.
source_locator: §6.1 Postmarketing Experience — Local Irritation: local irritation, erythema, mild pain, hematoma or ulceration may follow deep subcutaneous injection. §5.2/§6.1 Hemorrhage: bleeding is the chief complication and can occur at any site.
source_claim_supported: Local hematoma may follow deep subcutaneous heparin injection; clinically significant hemorrhage remains an important adverse effect requiring assessment.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication response, assess adverse effects, review pertinent data, and administer high-risk medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt all choices as comparable clinical interpretations.
Specified an isolated small local hematoma without other bleeding findings to exclude competing serious-bleeding actions.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current label for an isolated local hematoma. B and C contradict labeling; D overreacts without evidence of significant hemorrhage, HIT, or another discontinuation indication.
